conviction_note: Evidence is two-sided and mostly priced: rates have moved past what the Q2 guide assumed and used-car values softened (negative for the exit-NIM and Q4 credit language), while Ally's deposit repricing after the September hike was small and the EPS bar has been cut to 1.32-1.36 against a 1.48 whisper (positive). With the stock down about 16-17% since the July print and 5.7 vol points of put skew, the downside story is largely in the price, so p_up sits at 47. abs_move 5.5 is below the 6.91 event-implied move because Q3 is not a guidance-reset quarter (2027 comes in January), but well above the 2.39 historical median because the rate shock makes the NIM-exit language the swing factor. The findings sum to -0.9 and the scaled number is -0.33; both are small and point the same way.

Company guide: FY2026 NIM ex-OID 3.6-3.7% with exit above the top of the range, retail auto NCO 1.8-2.0%, consolidated NCO 1.2-1.3% (Q2 call https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-7-21-ally-financial-inc-stock/ ; reaffirmed at Barclays 2026-09-15 https://quartr.com/events/ally-financial-inc-ally-barclays-24th-annual-global-financial-services-conference_3YFVGbMp). I sized against about $1.34. Because the sources disagree, every size here is capped small.
positioning_check: Short interest 12.9M shares, about 4.3-4.8% of float, 4.8 days to cover at the 2026-08-14 FINRA settlement (3.6 at 07-31) per https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/ally/short-interest/ and https://fintel.io/s/us/ALLY. Not a crowded short. No October settlement was found. The sealed baseline has 25d skew at +5.74 vol points (downside paid), put/call OI 0.25, event-implied move 6.91%, spot 37.45, -6.1% over 20 days, -20.7% from the 52-week high and 4.1% above the low. Earnings Whispers shows a -15.8% post-earnings drift since the 2026-07-21 print.

findings.finding: Rates have moved past what Ally's guide assumed. On the Q2 call (2026-07-21) management said its forward curve as of June 30 assumed one hike in September 2026 and another in early 2027. Since then the Fed hiked 25bp on 2026-09-16, the 10-year reached about 5.2% on 2026-09-25 (highest since 2007), and as of 2026-10-19 the market prices a December 2026 hike at about 75%, pulling the second hike forward. The 10-Q describes Ally's balance sheet as structurally liability-sensitive. That puts the 'exit above 3.7%' NIM language, which the stock trades on, at risk of being softened or pushed out on the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: NIM guidance is the line that moves this stock. The July 2026 print missed EPS by 1-2 cents with a reiterated NIM guide and fell 2.39%, then drifted down about 16%. The Barclays conference of 2026-09-15 guided Q3 NIM flat (rather than rising) and the shares fell about 3% that day (Goldesel). The baseline's largest reaction, +8.1% on 2026-04-17, came on a strong NIM print.
findings.why_not_priced: It is mostly priced: the stock is down about 16-17% since the print and fell about 11% in September as yields rose, and the skew pays for downside. What is not yet visible is whether management keeps or cuts the exit-NIM language. A cut is the remaining step, and the stock's position 4% above its 52-week low implies it is partly expected. Rates also eased in October (10-year about 5.06-5.13%, an October hold now priced at 83%), so the extreme scenario has faded.
findings.independence: Rates data from Trading Economics (2026-09-25 item and stream through 2026-10-19): https://tradingeconomics.com/united-states/government-bond-yield/news/586974 . Liability sensitivity from the 10-Q of June 30, 2026: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000040729/000004072926000017/ally-20260630.htm . Cox Automotive (2026-10-07) also cites 'interest rates climbing rapidly'. This is macro-to-company transmission that the company itself has not confirmed.

findings.finding: Ally's deposit repricing after the September hike was small and late. Its high-yield savings APY went from 3.00% (unchanged on 2026-09-22, CDs raised that day) to 3.10% by about 2026-09-30, and was still 3.10% on 2026-10-13. That is about a 40% beta on a 25bp hike, applied only in the last week of Q3. Q2 average retail deposit yield was 3.12%, so Q3 deposit cost is likely flat. This supports the flat Q3 NIM guide and slows how fast the hike hits Q4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Ally reported in Q2 that lower deposit costs drove NIM up 11bp quarter on quarter (2Q26 8-K). The baseline's largest positive reaction, +8.1% in April 2026, was on margin.
findings.why_not_priced: The market sold the stock as yields rose, which treats it as fully rate-exposed. If low deposit beta were priced, the September drawdown would have been smaller than the move in yields implies. These are consumer rate-tracking pages, not what analysts read.
findings.independence: DepositAccounts forum, 2026-09-22 (savings 3.00%, no change; CDs raised): https://www.depositaccounts.com/community/promos/63503-ally-rate-changes-9222026.html . ShopBack comparison (3.10% as of 2026-09-30): https://www.shopback.com/blog/finance/us-high-yield-savings-ally-vs-marcus-vs-sofi-vs-discover-2026 . All three are secondary sources. This partly offsets the first finding: it covers the Q3 cost path, while that finding covers the forward guide.

findings.finding: Ally pre-released parts of the quarter at Barclays on 2026-09-15: Q3 NIM roughly flat versus Q2's 3.63% ex-OID (it had previously been expected to rise) and about $20M of Q3 lease losses from Stellantis plug-in hybrid recalls. FY NIM (3.6-3.7%, exit above the top) and retail auto NCO (1.8-2.0%) were reaffirmed. Consensus appears to have fallen from about $1.43-1.47 to $1.32-1.36 since.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The shares fell about 3% on the conference day (Goldesel, 2026-09-15). These items sit inside what the company has already guided.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced: it was said publicly, the stock reacted, and estimates came down. It is filed so the panel sees what the print should already contain. Only a lease loss well above $20M, or a NIM below about 3.60%, would be news.
findings.independence: Quartr summary of the same conference (FY NIM guide, Stellantis residual losses continuing through 2026, retail auto NCO 1.8-2.0%): https://quartr.com/events/ally-financial-inc-ally-barclays-24th-annual-global-financial-services-conference_3YFVGbMp . Same event, so these count as one finding.

findings.finding: Used-vehicle values weakened in September. The Manheim index was 205.9, down 1.1% from August and 0.6% from a year earlier (unadjusted: -1.3% month on month, -1.2% year on year), with 'steeper-than-normal September depreciation'. Cox cut its year-end 2026 forecast from +2% to +0.2%. Ally's Q2 net lease depreciation was already $269M against $216M a year earlier. Lower values pressure lease remarketing gains and auto loss severity heading into the seasonally worst Q4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Credit and NCO commentary was a driver at the September 2024 Barclays conference (cited in TheFly headline) and in Q3 2025, when retail auto NCO was 1.88% (down 36bp year on year) and the stock rose 3.56%.
findings.why_not_priced: The Manheim index is widely followed, so this is partly priced through the September selloff. The quantitative read-through to Ally's Q4 NCO and lease gains will only appear in the outlook given on the call.
findings.independence: Q2 lease depreciation from the 10-Q income statement: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000040729/000004072926000017/ally-20260630.htm . This is an industry proxy, not an Ally number.

findings.finding: Capital One's auto net charge-off rate was 1.66% in August 2026 (30+ day delinquency 4.54%), against 1.54% for its Q3 2025 quarter. That suggests peer auto losses ticked up year on year into Q3, whereas Ally's Q2 retail auto NCO was down 18bp year on year at 1.57%. Ally's Q3 2025 retail auto NCO was 1.88%, so a Q3 2026 rate at or above that would break its streak of year-on-year improvement.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Year-on-year NCO improvement was a selling point in the Q2 2026 call and the Q3 2025 beat (+3.56%).
findings.why_not_priced: Capital One's monthly 8-Ks are watched, but the read-across to Ally's retail auto book is indirect. The comparison is a single month against a quarter, so it is noisy. Ally's own FY guide of 1.8-2.0% already allows for second-half normalization.
findings.independence: Capital One's Q3 2025 auto NCO of 1.54% from its Q3 2025 earnings coverage: https://autoremarketing.com/subprime/capital-ones-3q-auto-originations-climb-double-digits . This is a peer proxy, and it lands inside Ally's guided range.

findings.finding: The EPS bar has been reset lower going into the print. Earnings Whispers shows $1.32 consensus against a $1.48 whisper, and the iTiger preview (2026-10-13) shows $1.36, below the $1.43-1.47 still on older pages. For reference, Q3 2025 adjusted EPS was $1.15 against a $1.01 consensus and Q2 2026 was $1.21. A 2025-style seasonal step-up from Q2 (+16%) less the $20M lease loss lands at about $1.35, which is at the bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q3 2025 a 14% EPS beat bought +3.56%. In Q2 2026 a 1-2 cent miss with a held guide bought -2.39%, followed by a large drift down. Beats with a held guide have been bought modestly.
findings.why_not_priced: If the lowered bar were fully reflected, the skew would be flatter and the stock would not be near its 52-week low. The whisper sits 16 cents above consensus, which suggests buy-side expectations are higher than the published bar, so a modest beat may be needed rather than a 'clean' one.
findings.independence: Q3 2025 baseline: https://www.zacks.com/stock/news/2772078/ally-gains-on-q3-earnings-beat-yy-revenue-growth-provision-dip . The size is capped because the bar itself is disputed.

findings.finding: Regions Financial beat its Q3 2026 consensus on 2026-10-16 (adjusted EPS $0.73 vs $0.66 expected), with interest-bearing deposit costs flat at 1.70% against 1.69% in Q2 despite the September hike. That is an early read that bank deposit costs did not jump in Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None specific; sector read-through is usually modest.
findings.why_not_priced: Regions is a branch-funded regional with a very different deposit base from Ally's online bank. The read-across is weak and is already in sector prices.
findings.independence: Regions 3Q26 release: https://s202.q4cdn.com/476346942/files/content_files/3Q26-Press-Release_Website.pdf . This is a different business model, so it is a proxy only.

findings.finding: Ally resumed buybacks: $148M in Q2 2026, nearly $300M year to date, with CET1 at 10.1%. At a price about 20% below the 52-week high, continued repurchases are accretive. No new authorization or volume guide has been given.
findings.why_not_priced: Known. Only a step-up in pace or a new authorization would be news. Higher rates also reduce AOCI, which could constrain capital.
findings.independence: Barclays conference summary confirms buybacks resumed: https://quartr.com/events/ally-financial-inc-ally-barclays-24th-annual-global-financial-services-conference_3YFVGbMp

outside_window.finding: The FOMC meeting of 2026-10-27/28 and the expected December hike (about 75% priced) drive Ally's Q4 deposit costs after the exit window.

baseline_tension: The negatives (a rate path beyond the guide, weaker used-car values, a peer's auto NCO up year on year) agree with the +5.74 put skew and the -16% drift since July, so they are largely priced. The two positives (low deposit beta, a lowered EPS bar against a higher whisper) cut against the skew. Net, the findings lean slightly negative and p_up sits just under 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (disputed bar, $1.32-1.47): the bar-dependent positioning finding was cut from +0.8 to +0.5.
Rule 3 (own caveat must reach the number): the rate-path finding was cut from -1.5 to -1.2, because yields eased in October and an October hold is now priced.
Rule 5 (proxy evidence): the deposit-APY finding rests on secondary consumer sources, so it was trimmed from +0.5 to +0.4. The Manheim and Capital One proxies stayed small.
Rule 6 (inside the guided range): the pre-released Barclays items were moved toward 0, from -0.2 to -0.1.
Rule 7 (positioning): short interest was checked at 4.3-4.8% of float, not crowded, so the negatives were not shrunk for squeeze risk. The skew pushed p_up from 48 to 47.
The sums are equal (-0.9) by coincidence: the individual sizes moved.
